# Model Tree

**Example status — excerpt:** schemas isolate tree/address behavior; use
[Getting Started](../getting-started.qmd) for a tested lifecycle.

The schema passed to `Model(...)` becomes a tree. The singleton root represents
one processed observation, `Branch(...)` nodes define child contexts, and leaf
tensorfields represent typed source values.

Read this page as the public structural model: what the nodes mean, how
addresses are formed, and where context can interact. Read
[Data Flow](data-flow.qmd) first if preprocessing, tensorfields, decoding, and
prediction output are still unfamiliar.

## Read A Schema As A Tree

```{python .marimo}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model(
    name="order",
    d_model=64,
    n_layers=2,
    n_heads=4,
    embed=True,
    source_channel=rf.Category(active=False, size=16),
    line_items=rf.Branch(
        length=32,
        embed=True,
        sku=rf.Category(size=2048),
        quantity=rf.Number,
        price=rf.Number(mask=rf.Mask(rate=0.15, reconstruct=True)),
    ),
    returned=rf.Category(mask=True, size=2),
)

model
```

```text
order                         root branch, exported embedding
|-- source_channel            inactive category leaf
|-- line_items                repeated branch, exported embedding
|   |-- sku                   category leaf
|   |-- quantity              number leaf
|   `-- price                 number leaf, masked reconstruction
`-- returned                  supervised category target
```

The schema says that one order contains a repeated list of line items and a
return target. `source_channel` remains in the serializable schema but is
inactive. The line-item fields share item coordinates, and the branch can emit
its own representation before the order is represented at the root.

## Node Kinds

| Node kind | Created by | Public role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Root | `Model(..., name=...)` | Singleton context for one processed observation. |
| Branch | `Branch(..., length=...)` | Bounded child context whose aligned values can interact before pooling to its parent. |
| Leaf tensorfield | `Number`, `Category`, `Set`, `Hash`, `DateParts`, `Text`, `Vector`, `Boolean` | Binds and represents a typed source value; optionally decodes a prediction. |

The generated root is named `record` by default. `Model(name="order", ...)`
renames it, but it remains a singleton with internal length 1. Repeated root
data belongs in a child `Branch(length=...)`.

Only leaves encode typed values. A branch gives descendants shape and context;
by default, its name selects the same-named child collection from the processed
observation. Any node can use a node-relative `query` to select a different
structural path. See [Binding Data](binding-data.qmd) for direct, query, and
preprocessor input contracts.

## Addresses Are Stable Locations

Every node has a slash-delimited `rf.Address` derived from its schema path:

| Node | Address object | String form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| root | `rf.Address("order")` | `order` |
| line-items branch | `rf.Address("order", "line_items")` | `order/line_items` |
| price leaf | `rf.Address("order", "line_items", "price")` | `order/line_items/price` |
| target leaf | `rf.Address("order", "returned")` | `order/returned` |

Addresses identify nodes in displays, metric names, mutation predicates, and
prediction dictionaries. They describe the model contract. A preprocessor or
explicit leaf query can select a differently named source value without
changing its address.

## Branches Define Alignment And Context

A branch is more than an object-key namespace. It defines a coordinate space
shared by descendant leaves.

For two line items, `sku`, `quantity`, and `price` all have two corresponding
positions. The first value in each leaf describes the first item. Padding extends
that dimension to `line_items.length`; overflow controls values beyond the
configured length.

Child values can interact inside their branch before the branch representation
flows to its parent. Nested branches repeat the pattern:

```text
customer
|-- login_sessions[]
|   `-- events[]
`-- transactions[]
```

Events interact inside a session; session representations interact in the
login-session context; the pooled result reaches the customer. Transactions
have a separate local context before their pooled result reaches the same root.

This hierarchy does not automatically join values across sibling branches.
Identity matching or alignment across contexts must be represented explicitly
in the observation shape or preprocessing.

## Schema Roles And Mutations

Node settings change how a schema participates in learning and prediction:

| Setting | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `mask=0.15` | Uses a learned mask at sampled positions during training, without a direct reconstruction loss. |
| `mask=rf.Mask(rate=0.15, reconstruct=True)` | Reconstructs sampled positions. |
| `mask=rf.Mask(rate=0.15, skip=True)` | Omits sampled inputs from tensorization and routing during training. |
| `mask=True` | Always skips a node and reconstructs its leaf values as supervised targets. |
| branch `mask=...` | Applies one decision atomically to the active descendant subtree. |
| `embed=True` | Emits an embedding at a root, branch, or leaf address during prediction. |
| `active=False` | Retains a node in the schema while excluding it from execution. |

The complete learning-role contract belongs to
[Learning Modes & Embeddings](embeddings.qmd). In particular, embedding export
does not create a reconstruction objective. Structural skipping and a learned
mask are distinct encoder effects selected through the same policy.

The tree is also the selection surface for explicit schema changes:

| Method | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `model.update(predicate, **values)` | Change selected node configuration. |
| `model.extend(predicate, new_field, ...)` | Add children under one selected branch. |
| `model.delete(predicate)` | Permanently remove selected nodes and descendants. |
| `model.reset(predicate)` | Reinitialize selected runtime modules while keeping schema values. |
| `model.override(predicate, **values)` | Apply temporary changes inside a context manager. |

Use predicates such as `rf.where("name") == "price"`,
`rf.where("type") == "number"`, or an exact address to select nodes. Mutations
rebuild the runtime graph and reuse state whose names and shapes remain
compatible. They are blocked while Lightning owns an active train, validation,
test, or prediction loop.

Compatibility is mechanical, not semantic: reusing a tensor of the same shape
does not prove that a changed query, preprocessor contract, or field meaning is
safe. Validate and save schema mutations as new model artifacts.

## Architecture Internals

The public concepts above are sufficient for ordinary model design. The
remaining sections explain the tensor shapes and routing that implement them.
They are most useful for debugging, performance work, and tensorfield extension.

The runtime tree is backed by Pydantic schema models and installed node
objects. Vector payloads are routed internally in `Parcel` objects; a decoder's
`heritage` is the path of contexts it can gather for one target.

### Tensor Shapes

Each branch adds a dimension to descendant leaf arrays. For
`order/line_items/price`, the inherited schema shape is:

```text
order.length       -> 1
line_items.length  -> 32
leaf shape             -> (1, 32)
```

At runtime, a scalar tensorfield carries arrays such as:

```text
state      (batch, 1, 32)  - valued, null, padded, masked, or reserved other
content    (batch, 1, 32)  - datatype-specific content
trainable  (batch, 1, 32)  - whether a retained answer may contribute to loss
present    (batch, 1, 32)  - whether the coordinate participates in routing
inferred   (batch, 1, 32)  - whether prediction requested reconstruction
```

Some types add content dimensions. `Vector` content includes the configured
vector width; `Set` content includes its capacity dimension. The authoritative
state vocabulary and public output contract are documented in
[Built-In Data Types](data-types.qmd#value-state).

Leaf embedders convert present state and content into compact `d_model`-wide
payloads, then RelFlow scatters them back into fixed schema geometry:

```text
leaf embedding payload  (batch, ..., d_model)
array embedding payload (batch, ..., d_model)
```

The repeated dimensions before `d_model` come from branch ancestors.

### Forward Pass

A forward pass traverses the tree from leaves upward, then decodes selected
leaves from the context available along their path.

1. Raw records have already been preprocessed and bound directly or through
   explicit node-relative queries.
2. Arrow resolves every mask policy against pristine values, then creates
   separate input and target `RaggedField` projections.
3. Datatype codecs tensorize those projections once. Present leaf coordinates
   embed state and content and send vector parcels to their parent branches.
4. Branch encoders run from the deepest branches toward the root. Each branch
   combines child parcels, applies configured local attention, pools the child
   context, and sends one representation to its parent.
5. Nodes configured with `embed=True` make their representations available to
   prediction output.
6. Leaves compiled as fitting objectives, deterministic prediction decodes, or
   embedding outputs gather context and run their decoders.
7. During train, validation, or test, tensorfield losses and metrics use retained
   trainable targets. During prediction, writers serialize decoded values and
   configured embeddings.

### Pooling And Heritage

Branch pooling compresses a child context before it flows upward. After local
attention, learned-query cross-attention produces the branch vector passed to
the parent.

Decoder pooling builds context for a leaf. A leaf's **heritage** contains the
addresses on its root-to-leaf path. For `order/line_items/price`:

```text
order
order/line_items
order/line_items/price
```

The decoder gathers available outgoing parcels from that path and pools them
into the target leaf shape. The default `pooling="query"` uses learned-query
cross-attention. `pooling="mean"` repeats the mean heritage context for each
target slot.

This lets a decoded leaf use ancestor contexts and visible information in its
own branch. A learned mask can communicate masked state without its original
content. A skipped coordinate has no input parcel at all; its original value
exists only in the target projection when reconstruction is enabled.
